sections.heading: Roof Replacement
body: Some roofs are past saving. The shingles curl at the edges, bare patches show where the granules wore off, and you've had a leak in one room and then another.
Once the damage is spread across the whole roof, every patch becomes one more seam for water to find. You end up paying for repairs on a roof that is already finished.
A replacement starts with a free estimate. I look at the roof, tell you what I see, and give you the price before any work begins.
Then we tear off the old roof and put on the new one. Most house roofs go on in a day or two, depending on the size and the weather.

sections.quote: Eric and his team did an excellent job on a tear-off roofing job for me. They completed everything on time and on budget. Great communication and very prompt. I will definitely use them again.

sections.heading: Roof Repair
body: You find shingles in the yard after a windy night. Or a brown stain spreads across the ceiling and you can't tell where the water is coming from.

A few missing shingles expose the layer underneath, and that layer was never meant to face the weather. A leak is harder, because water travels along the decking and shows up a long way from where it got in.
We find the spot where the water gets in and fix that, not just the stain. If the roof is simply worn out, I'll tell you that, too.

sections.heading: When Insurance Is Part of the Job
body: Hail or wind takes shingles off, your insurance company sends an adjuster, and suddenly you're learning a process you never wanted to learn.
I walk the roof with you and explain what the work involves. I answer your questions about the next steps, and I'm there to talk through the roofing side when your adjuster comes out.
I can't tell you what your insurance company will pay, and no honest roofer can. The claim is between you and your insurer. My part is making sure everyone is looking at the same roof.

hero.h1: Roof Replacement in Wichita, KS — Better Solutions Roofing & Construction
hero.sub: When shingles curl, leaks show up in more than one place or a storm hits the whole roof, repairs stop paying off. I'm Eric, and I'll tell you whether your roof needs replacing. Call me for a free quote.

sections.heading: When a Roof Is Past Repairing
body: A roof wears out slowly, and then all at once. The signs usually show up together:
list: Shingles curling, cracking or missing across more than one slope
Bare patches, and gritty granules washing into your gutters
Leaks in more than one spot, or one that keeps coming back
Daylight, or dark staining, in the attic
Hail or wind damage over the whole roof, not one corner
tail: The reason a repair stops working is simple. Old shingles go brittle, and a brittle shingle cracks when it's lifted, so a patch turns into a new place for water to get in.
If the damage is in one spot and the rest of the roof is sound, that's a [repair](/roof-repair-wichita-ks/), and I'll say so. A replacement is for the roof that's done.

items.text: New underlayment goes down, and flashing and vents are set around chimneys, walls and pipes.

items.title: Clean up.

sections.heading: Comparing Quotes
body: If you have more than one quote, make them match up. Ask each roofer the same questions:
list: Does the price include tearing off the old roof, or does it go over it?
What happens if the deck is rotted, and what does each board cost?
Are flashing, vents and drip edge replaced, or reused?
Are gutters in the price, or separate?
Who cleans up, and how?
tail: A low number that leaves these out isn't low. I'm glad to go through any quote with you.

items.q: Do you replace roofs on new construction?

items.q: Do I have to be home?

items.q: Can you replace just part of a roof?
items.a: Yes, when the damage is limited to one section and the rest is in good shape. That's a repair, and I'll tell you if it's the better choice.

sections.heading: Shingles Lost in the Wind
body: You come home after a windy night and there are shingles in the yard, or you spot a bare patch from the street. A missing shingle leaves the layer underneath exposed, and that layer was never meant to take the sun and rain.
Wind gets under a shingle whose seal has aged, and lifts it. Once one goes, the shingles beside it are easier to lift.
We replace what blew off, check the shingles around it and make sure the new ones seal down. It's usually a small job, and it's worth doing before the next storm.

sections.heading: Water Through the Ceiling
body: A stain on the ceiling is rarely under the hole in the roof. Water gets in at one spot, runs along the decking or a rafter, and drips out somewhere else.
That's why patching above the stain so often fails. The usual culprits are flashing around chimneys, walls and vents, cracked pipe boots, and valleys where two slopes meet.
A bead of caulk can hide a bad flashing job for a season. It doesn't fix it. We start at the stain, work upward and outward until we find where the water gets in, and repair that.

sections.quote: Eric was easy to work with and responded quickly when we had water coming through our ceiling. He was dedicated to finding a solution and went above and beyond, patching up other issues he noticed on our roof!

sections.heading: Vents and Flashing
body: The small parts of a roof do a lot of the work. Vents let attic air out, flashing seals the joints, and rubber boots wrap the pipes that come through.
Those parts wear out before the shingles do. When one fails, water finds it first, so replacing a worn vent or resetting flashing is often the whole repair.

sections.heading: Why Kansas Roofs Need Repairs
body: Wichita roofs take a lot. Spring storms bring hail and straight-line wind, summer sun bakes the shingles, and a freeze and thaw in winter works water into every small gap.
A roof that's a few years old can lose shingles in one gust, and the damage rarely stays small if it's left. A repair done early costs a fraction of what the same leak does after a season of rain.

sections.heading: Repair or Replace?
body: Repair makes sense when the damage is in one place and the rest of the roof is sound. Replacement makes sense when the trouble is everywhere: shingles curling across several slopes, granules piling up in the gutters, leaks in more than one spot.
I'll tell you which one you're looking at, and why.
When replacement is the honest answer, here's what [replacing the whole roof](/roof-replacement-wichita-ks/) involves.

sections.heading: What a Repair Visit Looks Like
body: We look at more than the spot you pointed to. Older shingles go brittle, and the ones next to the damage tell us how much life the roof has left.
Then you hear what we found and what the fix will cost before the work begins. If something bigger is coming, you'll know about it before it turns into an emergency.

sections.quote: Amazing at what they do. Fast and quick service. They will help with any of your needs and you can trust them.

sections.heading: After a Storm
body: If hail or wind brought you here, your insurance company may be part of the repair. I can walk the roof with you and your adjuster and talk through the roofing side.
What a policy covers and what it pays is between you and your insurer. I'll tell you what I see on the roof.

items.q: How soon should I fix missing shingles?
items.a: As soon as you reasonably can. Exposed underlayment lets water in, and the next wind or rain makes it worse.

items.q: Why is the ceiling stained when the roof looks fine?
items.a: Water travels from where it gets in. Flashing, vent boots and valleys are the first places to check.

items.q: Will new shingles match my old ones?
items.a: Close, usually, but not perfectly. Sun fades shingles, so new ones can look a shade different at first.

items.q: Does it cost anything for you to look?
items.a: No. Estimates and inspections are free.

why: Your customers already make your case on Google: 87 five-star reviews, again and again naming Eric for answering questions and leaving the yard clean.
Your website hides it. On a phone it runs off the screen, the Services button goes nowhere, and none of those reviews appear on it.
So we built this site around Eric: a headline that says roofing company in Wichita, a page each for roof replacement and roof repair, and your reviews beside what they prove.

cards.title: Homepage
cards.why: The page Google reads to learn who you are, and the first thing a customer sees on a phone.
problems: The big headline on your homepage is your company name, so Google can't tell you're a roofing company in Wichita the way people search it.
On a phone the site is twice as wide as the screen. The headline is cut off and your phone number breaks across two lines.
The Services button in your menu goes nowhere, and a financing box covers the first screen.
The reviews on the page repeat three names twice, and the Google reviews that name Eric aren't there.
fixes: A headline that says roofing company in Wichita, KS, right at the top.
A page that fits a phone, with your number one tap away.
A menu where every button opens a page, and nothing over the top of the page.
Real reviews from your customers, each beside the point it proves.
cards.alsoAdd: Hourly speed monitoring that keeps your site fast for visitors on phones, and speed is something Google uses to rank you.
